observations: Photo 0 and Photo 1 show the same electronic keyboard wrapped in clear plastic.
The keyboard has 61 keys, with white and black keys arranged in standard layout.
The front panel includes a central display screen, several buttons, and a green circular logo above the screen.
The keyboard appears to be in a store or workshop setting, with other keyboards visible in the background.
The plastic wrap is intact, suggesting the item is new or well-preserved.
No visible damage to the keys or casing is apparent from the photos.

claims.claim: high-quality sound, responsive playability, and versatile...
claims.evidence: These are subjective performance claims that cannot be verified from photos alone.

risks.risk: The keyboard may be non-functional or have internal damage not visible in photos.
risks.proof: A video showing the keyboard powered on, keys responding, and sound output.

risks.risk: The plastic wrap may be old or the item may have been previously used, despite appearance.
risks.proof: Close-up of the plastic wrap edges and any signs of wear or residue.
risks.if_unproven: priced as used, with potential for lower value

risks.risk: The keyboard may be a counterfeit or rebranded unit.
risks.proof: Clear photo of the model number and serial number, ideally from the back or underside.

proof_requests: Close-up of the sticker with the model number, usually inside the lid or on the bottom.
Video of the keyboard powered on and playing notes.
Close-up of the back or underside to check for model number and serial number.
Photo of the plastic wrap edges to check for wear or residue.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
